---
title: "Models"
---

`lm()` and `glm()` pass the piped table to the php-stats extension's
`stats_lm()` and `stats_glm()`. The extension reads factor levels from the
table, builds the model matrix, and returns coefficients, standard errors, and
fit statistics in the same order as R.

```php
$table |> lm('y ~ x + group');
$table |> glm('passed ~ hours', family: 'binomial');   // also 'poisson', link:
```

Both need php-stats with the formula functions. Without the extension they
throw an exception that says so.
